title: Liberty UI style board
prompt: A UI style board for Liberty Vanilla+, a grounded GTA IV-era remaster set in a cold, rainy, New York-like city in 2008. The background must read as a remastered 2008 third-person game screenshot: modest angular urban geometry, weathered brick, elevated railway, wet pavement, muted grey-brown grading and warm street lamps, restrained game-rendered lighting rather than a cinematic photorealistic photograph. A generic original player figure may be viewed from behind. Preserve the established screen anchors. In the TOP-RIGHT corner, within a small safe margin, place a compact off-white current-weapon silhouette with the exact ammo text "17 / 68" immediately below it; directly underneath, place two thin, compact health and armour indicators, muted sage-green for health and pale desaturated blue-grey for armour. This entire weapon/ammo/health/armour group must be at the TOP RIGHT, never in a lower corner. Keep a small circular radar at the BOTTOM LEFT with simple monochrome street blocks and a player arrow; no compass letters, no labels. In the centre, show a radial weapon selector with exactly six segments: sidearm, two long guns, melee, thrown, and an entirely blank empty segment. Use simple white line-art weapon silhouettes and a restrained muted amber edge on the selected segment. Place a compact two-column carried / vehicle-trunk inventory panel at right-centre, below and clearly separate from the top-right HUD. All other placeholder text must be short illegible lines. Use compact off-white condensed lettering with a thin dark outline, flat crisp monochrome icons, dark translucent grey/black menu surfaces, restrained amber/orange/red accents, sharp edges, minimal decoration and generous spacing. Match the understated, utilitarian GTA IV-era visual language with original artwork. No health crosses or large boxed HUD cards, no decorative distressed texture on UI, no readable text except "17 / 68", no game logos, no copied game artwork, no copyrighted characters, no neon gradients, no rounded mobile-app cards, no glossy glass.
intendedUse: Concept for T-045 weapon wheel, T-046 trunk UI and T-049 HUD: one style board that sets the Liberty Vanilla+ UI language before Slice C.
styleConstraints: Must look like it belongs in GTA IV (2008, Liberty City, late-2000s New York analogue), remastered today; not GTA V, not GTA Online
Cold, grey, overcast, wet-city palette; grime, wear and dirt are welcome; warm artificial light against cold surroundings
Grounded and realistic, photographic material detail; no stylisation, no cartoon, no painterly look unless the request says so
Late-2000s objects, technology, signage and typography of that era, without real brands

UI and icons: preserve a GTA IV-era visual language with original artwork; compact monochrome icons and off-white condensed lettering with thin dark outlines; dark translucent grey/black menu surfaces and restrained amber/orange/red accents; thin muted sage-green health and desaturated blue-grey armour indicators; sharp purposeful shapes and minimal decoration
Owner-directed HUD placement: current weapon, ammo, health and armour are grouped in the top-right corner; radar remains bottom-left; menus must not overlap these anchors
prohibited: Real brand names, logos, trademarks or copyrighted characters
Rockstar, GTA, Take-Two or any game's logos, UI or artwork
Readable text unless the request gives the exact text
Neon gradients, glossy mobile-app UI, large rounded cards, live-service styling
Modern (post-2010) phones, cars, fashion or technology
Cartoon, anime, comic or exaggerated gore styles
Lighting or shadows baked into tiling textures (unless the request asks for it)
Perspective or visible camera angle in textures meant to tile (textures are flat, orthographic)
Weapon/ammo/health/armour HUD in any lower corner; oversized boxed HUD cards or health-cross icons
Compass letters, radar labels, or readable text other than the exact ammo text 17 / 68
Cinematic photographic background, modern photorealistic rendering, or decorative distressed texture on the UI
